raw.assessment: The incumbent provides reservations, telephone/in-person changes and staffed key collection; eleven groups obtained a weekly booking. It does not establish the target: needs are unmeasured, three access conflicts occurred, and administration averaged 127.5 minutes weekly. The concrete limiting observation is 68% reserved capacity alongside declined requests concentrated on Tuesday/Thursday evenings. This weakens an aggregate-capacity explanation but does not demonstrate usable spare capacity: acceptable alternatives and most equipment requirements are unknown. Four groups rehearsing elsewhere likewise cannot establish successful access under undocumented arrangements. Late or unattended sessions do not establish that their time could reliably be reassigned.

openings.claim: Inherited booking times and unrecorded compatibility requirements may leave a feasible allocation undiscovered; aggregate spare capacity alone cannot establish this.
openings.delta: Test whether unused time can meet actual needs while protecting every requested weekly minimum, rather than treating nominal vacancies as interchangeable.
openings.prediction: A schedule using declared acceptable windows, necessary equipment and durations can either meet the 90% needs target plus every required weekly minimum, or expose a specific time/equipment bottleneck despite overall vacancies.
openings.probe: Use short contact conversations to record weekly needs, acceptable windows, equipment and minimum useful duration. Construct a paper allocation within the two rooms and existing staffed hours, preserving both performances. Compare its achievable coverage with existing bookings; count a 60-minute entitlement separately from a longer rehearsal need. Make no booking changes during this feasibility probe.
assumptions: Contacts can accurately describe their groups' needs.
Feasibility is unknown; no group is assumed willing to accept shorter rehearsals or different times.

openings.claim: A desk-authoritative ledger with unique reservation references and explicit replacement confirmations may reduce contradictory access expectations.
openings.delta: Give each telephone or in-person change one traceable current reservation; mark the online copy with its synchronization time.
openings.prediction: Conflicts caused by stale or duplicate confirmations decline, while logging costs may offset any reduction in clarification work.
openings.probe: Pilot the ledger within existing bookings and staffed hours; read back room, date, time and superseded reference on each change. Record conflict causes and all administration minutes for eight weeks, testing fewer than two conflicts and a weekly average at most 120 minutes.
assumptions: The desk and volunteer consistently consult the same ledger.
Two double-expectation incidents have unknown causes, so reconciliation may not prevent them.

raw.assessment: The observations do not establish a shortage of total room capacity: acceptable windows, equipment needs and usable attendance remain unknown. Both openings are hypotheses; neither establishes that the eight-week targets are feasible.

openings.claim: Groups may share indispensable musicians, making some nominally separate reservations mutually unusable and contributing to late or missed sessions.
openings.delta: Treat the scheduling unit as compatible group attendance, alongside room availability, rather than assuming each group is independent.
openings.prediction: If shared personnel are a material cause, contacts will identify overlapping indispensable attendance requirements corresponding to late or missed sessions; moving those bookings to acceptable nonoverlapping windows should improve attendance without adding room-hours.
openings.probe: During the available short conversations, ask contacts which other groups share essential attendees and whether this caused any of the 14 affected sessions. Record only group-pair conflicts. If supported, trial one mutually accepted schedule exchange while protecting every requested weekly 60-minute entitlement and the performances; compare attendance at the affected sessions.
assumptions: Some groups may share essential attendees; this is unobserved.
An acceptable exchange exists and can be recorded consistently through existing telephone or desk channels.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: allocating requested 60-minute weekly entitlements before allocating optional extensions can prevent inherited 90-minute bookings from stranding useful rehearsal time.
openings.delta: Separate guaranteed access from additional duration, using stated rehearsal needs to decide extensions rather than inheriting every booking length.
openings.prediction: Where contiguous fragments and acceptable windows align, this allocation admits previously excluded groups while retaining sufficient longer sessions; otherwise it reveals that shortening bookings cannot resolve the bottleneck.
openings.probe: Use contacts' actual duration, window and equipment requirements to draft one weekly allocation within existing staffed hours, preserving performances. Compare satisfied needs and excluded groups with the inherited allocation, and count administration time before any agreed trial. Accept telephone and in-person changes, with one authoritative booking record.
assumptions: Some 90-minute reservations can be shortened without losing required rehearsal value.
A 60-minute entitlement does not by itself count as meeting a group's full stated need.
Guaranteed slots remain available to every requesting group; existing equipment and zero new fees are retained.

openings.claim: Unrecorded compatibility and inherited 90-minute blocks may hide feasible access.
openings.discriminator: Compare existing allocation, needs-matched allocation, and 60-minute entitlements followed by extensions; nominal vacancies and entitlements do not establish full needs coverage.
openings.probe: Interview contacts about needs, windows, equipment and useful durations; compare paper allocations and administration before agreed changes.
openings.uncertainty: Usable alternatives, beneficial shortening and target feasibility remain unknown.

openings.claim: One desk-authoritative ledger and replacement confirmations may reduce contradictory access expectations.
openings.discriminator: Fewer stale or duplicate confirmations, weighed against logging time.
openings.probe: Pilot unique references, room/date/time and superseded-reference readback, and online synchronization timestamps; log conflict causes and all administration for eight weeks.
openings.uncertainty: Consistent consultation is required; two conflicts have unexplained causes.

openings.claim: Shared indispensable musicians may make separate bookings mutually unusable.
openings.discriminator: Group-pair attendance conflicts explain affected late or missed sessions.
openings.fit: Preserves constraints with an accepted exchange.
openings.probe: Ask contacts about essential-member overlap in the 14 affected sessions; record group pairs only. If supported, trial one acceptable exchange and compare attendance.
openings.uncertainty: Overlap and an acceptable exchange are unobserved.

lineage.reason: With Z1; retains entitlement-first fragmentation hypothesis.

post_distill.decision: Probe feasibility before allocation changes. Preserve two rooms, 24 staffed hours, every requested weekly 60-minute entitlement, offline channels, equipment, zero new fees and both performances. Test eight-week coverage >=90%, conflicts <2 and administration <=120 minutes/week; success is unestablished.
